definitions.explanation: The taste of salt, or a seasoning style based primarily on salt rather than soy sauce, miso, or other flavorings.

examples.japanese: ラーメンは{塩味|しおみ}が{好|す}きだ。
このスープは{塩味|しおみ}が{足|た}りない。
examples.english: This soup doesn't have enough saltiness.

examples.japanese: {素材|そざい}の{味|あじ}を{活|い}かすなら、シンプルに{塩味|しおみ}だけで{調理|ちょうり}するのが{一番|いちばん}だ。
examples.english: If you want to bring out the natural flavor of the ingredients, the best approach is to cook with just salt seasoning.

notes:
A compound of {塩|しお} (salt) and {味|み} (taste/flavor). In the context of ramen and other dishes, {塩味|しおみ} refers to a salt-based broth or seasoning style, as opposed to {醤油|しょうゆ}{味|あじ} (soy sauce flavor), {味噌|みそ}{味|あじ} (miso flavor), or {豚骨|とんこつ} (pork bone broth).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {塩味|しおみ}のラーメン: salt-flavored ramen
- {塩味|しおみ}が{効|き}いている: has a good amount of salt flavor
- {塩味|しおみ}が{足|た}りない: not salty enough
- {塩味|しおみ}が{強|つよ}い: too salty
- {塩味|しおみ}ベース: salt-based (seasoning)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {塩味|しおあじ}: saltiness — same kanji, alternative reading; しおあじ focuses more on the taste sensation, while しおみ is used more as a seasoning category
- {塩分|えんぶん}: salt content — the amount of salt in food; a nutritional/health term
- {塩辛|しおから}い: salty (adjective) — describes food that has too much salt
